title: Mitigate variant misclassification causing cross-region reroute spirals
creator: Aisha Patel
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 a capacity-triggered fallback path interacted with a stale policy cache and an inconsistent variant compatibility map, causing a decaying oscillation where requests were rerouted across regions and to incompatible model variants. This produced elevated latencies (p95 +350ms), a spike in 5xxs for affected routes (~3.8% absolute increase), and visible user-facing slowdowns for multiple high-traffic tenants during a 42-minute window. Root cause: a race between policy rollout TTL refresh and variant-tag reconciliation that allowed an old mapping to be used as the canonical fallback target.
action_items: Add a synchronous variant-compatibility check in the routing decision path: verify model architecture + quantization schema before accepting a fallback target
Implement an epoched policy header (route_policy_epoch) that rejects stale policy cache entries older than N seconds to prevent silent acceptance
Deploy a short-circuit circuit-breaker that detects rapid bidirectional reroutes between two regions and forces a holdout to break oscillation
Enhance fallback telemetry: emit policy_version, variant_checksum, origin_region, chosen_region, and decision_reason for every fallback event to tracing and metrics
Add an automated CI regression that replays the incident repro (capacity drop + staggered policy refresh) against the smart-routing simulator
Create an integration test that validates fallback correctness across quantized variants (int8 vs fp16) to prevent incompatible mapping
Update the oncall runbook with explicit rollback steps for variant map changes and add a playbook section for oscillation detection and mitigation
Backfill 30 days of fallback decision logs to S3 for root-cause analysis and to support forensics requests
Schedule a cross-team design review (Runtime, Routing, Console) to validate rollout plan and telemetry schema before changes land
Perform a midnight canary rollout with throttled traffic and enhanced observability before global release
